questions.q: Which data factory environment should ever be connected to Git?
options: Only the development factory
All three — dev, test, and production
Only production, for auditability
None — Git integration should never be used with any environment
questions.explain: Only dev is Git-connected; test and production are updated exclusively through the release pipeline or a manually deployed ARM template, never authored or connected to Git directly.

questions.q: How do dev, test, and production end up with different configuration (like different storage account names) if they all deploy from the same ARM template?
options: Global parameters are overridden per environment at deployment time
Each environment requires a completely separate, manually maintained pipeline
The ARM template is manually edited before each deployment
Configuration can't actually differ between environments
questions.explain: Global parameters let the same pipeline logic reference environment-specific values, overridden through ARM template parameters at deployment time — no pipeline duplication required.

questions.q: Does Data Factory support publishing only a subset of your changes (cherry-picking)?
options: No — publishing includes everything in the collaboration branch, every time
Yes, you can select exactly which resources to publish
Only for pipelines, not for datasets or linked services
Only when using GitHub, not Azure Repos
questions.explain: Because entities depend on each other (triggers depend on pipelines, pipelines depend on datasets), partial publishing risks an inconsistent factory state — so Data Factory always publishes everything together.

questions.q: What's the recommended approach when you need a narrow, urgent fix without including unrelated in-progress work?
options: A dedicated hotfix process, not selective publishing
Manually editing the production factory directly
Deleting the unrelated in-progress work permanently
There's no way to handle this scenario
questions.explain: Since selective publishing isn't supported, Data Factory's recommended pattern for urgent narrow fixes is a dedicated hotfix process rather than cherry-picking changes.

questions.q: What's the recommended Key Vault practice across environments?
options: Use separate Key Vaults per environment, but keep the same secret names in each
Use one single shared Key Vault across dev, test, and production
Use different secret names in every environment for security
Key Vault can't be used across multiple environments at all
questions.explain: Separate Key Vaults per environment with matching secret names means you only need to parameterize the vault name itself, not every individual secret reference.
